title: The proper projection formula on the rational localizing categories
statement:
Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$ and let $p:X\to Y$ be proper. For
$A\in\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$ and $B\in\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))$ the projection
formula map

$$
(Rp_*A)\otimes^{\mathbf L}B\longrightarrow Rp_*(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}p^*B)
$$

is an isomorphism in $\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))$.

proof.text: Use the standing separated finite-type scheme setting, and the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings, throughout; no replacement by the category of discrete rational sheaves is made. These schemes are qcqs. For $T=X,Y$, the rational cases of the finite-Tor comparison give $\Dctf(T,\Lambda)=\Dbc(T,\Lambda)$ and equality of their localizing closures. Thus all the subsequent localizing restriction and determination statements, formulated using $\Dctf$, apply to precisely the categories in this statement.

source.place: first paragraph: interpretation of the rational localizing categories

proof.text: Apply the inverse-image restriction with $g=p$ and the proper-image restriction with $p$ as in the statement. The latter explicitly asserts that its hypotheses hold for $\Lambda=E,\Qlb$; it is not being applied only conditionally. Using Step 1, both functors are exact and preserve all small direct sums on the displayed localizing categories. Tensor closure, applied on both $X$ and $Y$, gives $A\otimes^{\mathbf L}p^*B\in\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$ and $(Rp_*A)\otimes^{\mathbf L}B\in\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))$. Applying $Rp_*$ to the former gives the other term in the target localizing category.

source.place: first paragraph: restrictions and both terms of the map

proof.text: Derived tensor is exact in each variable by the ringed-topos tensor statement. It preserves direct sums in each variable: the closed structure supplies $C\otimes^{\mathbf L}-\dashv\RHom(C,-)$, and the coproduct universal property gives preservation; symmetry gives the other variable. Since the localizing subcategories are full and their coproducts are ambient coproducts, these properties restrict to them. Together with Step 2 this proves that both sides of the projection map, with either input fixed, are exact functors preserving direct sums.

source.place: first paragraph and second paragraph: tensor exactness and direct sums

proof.text: The module pullback is the ringed-topos pullback. The Cartesian coefficient isomorphism identifies this pullback with exact inverse image, so in the present coefficient system the functor $Lp^*$ is the module pullback $p^*$.

source.place: first paragraph: canonical map and exact natural transformations; Stacks 0B56, 07A4, 07A6 and 0A8D

proof.text: Put $L=p^*$ and $R=Rp_*$. With derived counit $\varepsilon:LR\to1$, the canonical unbounded projection map $\pi_{A,B}$ is the adjoint transpose of $L(RA\otimes^{\mathbf L}B)\xrightarrow{\mu}LRA\otimes^{\mathbf L}LB\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_A\otimes1}A\otimes^{\mathbf L}LB$. The ringed projection-mate statement supplies this map for arbitrary unbounded inputs, natural in both variables, and states that it commutes with the canonical shift structures.

source.place: first paragraph: canonical map and exact natural transformations; Stacks 0B56, 07A4, 07A6 and 0A8D

proof.text: Give the exact functor $L$ its canonical shift isomorphisms and give $R$ the shift structure supplied by clause (iii) of the abstract adjunction-shift lemma. The unit and counit commute with these shifts, in particular $\varepsilon_{A[1]}=\varepsilon_A[1]\circ e_{L,RA}\circ L(e_{R,A})$. By the triangulated-right-adjoint statement, $R$ with this shift structure is exact; hence its restriction in Step 2 is exact on the full triangulated localizing subcategories.

source.place: first paragraph: canonical map and exact natural transformations; Stacks 0B56, 07A4, 07A6 and 0A8D

proof.text: The shift compatibility in the ringed projection-mate statement identifies the transpose at $(A[1],B)$ with the shift of the transpose at $(A,B)$, using the displayed counit formula and the shift compatibility of $\mu$; the same argument at $(A,B[1])$ gives compatibility in the second variable. Naturality and these shift identities make the components on every distinguished triangle a morphism of triangles, including the connecting square. Thus the determination lemma applies to the actual canonical map, with exact structures for which both functors are exact.

source.place: first paragraph: canonical map and exact natural transformations; Stacks 0B56, 07A4, 07A6 and 0A8D

proof.text: If $A\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ and $B\in\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$, clause (3) of the rational proper-base-change theorem says precisely that this canonical proper projection formula map is an isomorphism. Its standing-scheme, properness, and rational-coefficient hypotheses hold here.

source.place: second paragraph: bounded constructible base case

proof.text: Fix $B\in\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$, so in particular $B\in\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))$. By Steps 2--7 the functors $A\mapsto (Rp_*A)\otimes^{\mathbf L}B$ and $A\mapsto Rp_*(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}p^*B)$ have common codomain $\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))$, are exact and preserve direct sums, and $\pi_{-,B}$ is a natural transformation of exact functors. Step 8 gives invertibility on $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$. The determination lemma, using the equalities of Step 1, gives invertibility for every $A\in\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$ and this bounded $B$.

source.place: second paragraph: first fix B bounded and extend in A

proof.text: Now fix any $A\in\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$. By Steps 2--7 both functors of $B$ are exact and preserve direct sums, with the same target localizing category, and $\pi_{A,-}$ is a natural transformation of exact functors. By Step 9 it is an isomorphism for every bounded constructible $B$. Apply the determination lemma with source scheme $Y$ and target scheme $Y$, and the equalities of Step 1, to obtain invertibility for all $B\in\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))$. This is the required isomorphism in the full target localizing category.

source.place: second paragraph: fix A arbitrary and extend in B

proof_origin.place: both paragraphs; expanded tensor coproduct argument and canonical-mate shift check using Stacks Tags 06YU, 07A4, 07A6, 0B56, 0A8D
